title: Efficient Nudged Elastic Band Method using Neural Network Bayesian Algorithm Execution
experiments_summary: The study applied the NN-BAX method to Lennard-Jones (LJ) atomic systems with 7 and 38 atoms (LJ7 and LJ38). Local minima were identified using basin hopping, and classical NEB was run between pairs of minima to establish ground-truth MEPs. MEP stability was verified by perturbing image positions by σx ∈ [0, 0.1] Å and re-running NEB for 100 iterations. Four transitions of varying complexity were analyzed: LJ7 paths with 0 and 3 intermediate minima, and LJ38 paths with 0 and 1 intermediate minima. Classical NEB and NN-BAX NEB both used the ASE library, the string method, and the FIRE optimizer (dt=0.1, dtmax=1.0). EquiformerV2 (153M parameters), pre-trained on the OMat24 dataset, served as the neural network surrogate and was fine-tuned in a few-shot manner during each BAX iteration. In each BAX iteration, the model was trained for 50 epochs with batch size 2, using the AdamW optimizer (weight decay 0.001, gradient clipping at 100), initial learning rate 2×10⁻⁴, a cosine learning rate schedule with 1-epoch warmup, and EMA decay of 0.999. The MAE loss weighted forces four times more than energy. NEB was run on the current surrogate model, and a point was randomly sampled from the resulting path to query the true LJ potential and update the model. Convergence was defined by simultaneous satisfaction of a force criterion (fmax,BAX = n·fmax,classical, with n=2) and a model prediction error criterion (MAEi < 0.1), with a patience parameter p (p=2 or p=3 depending on the path). Performance was evaluated by comparing energy-versus-image profiles and PCA projections of predicted MEPs against classical NEB ground truth, and by measuring the reduction in number of LJ potential function evaluations. All computations were performed on a single NVIDIA Tesla A100 GPU.
